title: Troubleshooting Gurgling Drains and Trap Siphonage
description: When a sink gurgles while another fixture drains, the primary cause is often negative air pressure created by a restricted vent line rather than a simple main line clog. Plumbing vents maintain atmospheric pressure within the drainage system. If a vent stack becomes obstructed by debris or ice, flowing water creates a vacuum that pulls water out of nearby P-traps. This siphoning action leaves traps empty, allowing sewer gases to enter living spaces. Inspecting the vent terminal on the roof and checking for internal air restrictions restores balanced pressure and protects the trap seals.

Troubleshooting Gurgling Drains and Trap Siphonage

When a sink gurgles while another fixture drains, the primary cause is often negative air pressure created by a restricted vent line rather than a simple main line clog. Plumbing vents maintain atmospheric pressure within the drainage system. If a vent stack becomes obstructed by debris or ice, flowing water creates a vacuum that pulls water out of nearby P-traps. This siphoning action leaves traps empty, allowing sewer gases to enter living spaces. Inspecting the vent terminal on the roof and checking for internal air restrictions restores balanced pressure and protects the trap seals.
